In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
it is not yet possible to use a single metric to evaluate usability.
it is possible to make a statistical analysis of the usability data, and that this may be useful for test leaders in order to focus their attention on the most problematic areas.
it is possible to use a single metric for the measurement of usability, but that the single metric is a measure of the usability of the use case and not of the usability of an entire system.

The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to gain an indication of the usability problems of a product from the data collected during usability tests, and this can be done without a full-scale analysis of the data.
there is value to be found in analysing usability data, even when there are only a few data points, as long as the data is of good quality and collected in a systematic manner.
